Cairn stops being a place memories are kept and starts being a thing that knows
what this project currently believes, what stands behind each belief, and when
the world has moved out from under one.

Still an **alpha**. Nothing here is a stability promise.

## Highlights

**Project intelligence.** Cairn answers what the project believes now, not just
what was written down. Beliefs supersede one another, conflicts are reported as
conflicts rather than silently resolved, and a claim carries whether it was
verified and by what authority. Nothing here needs a model, an embedding, a
vector store or a graph database, and none was added — every answer is a
deterministic function of recorded state, which is what lets two machines that
have never met agree.

**Compression-safe continuity, verified against live agents.** When an agent
compacts its context, Cairn writes a checkpoint before the boundary and hands it
back afterwards. `continuity_mode` tells you honestly which of those an
integration actually does:

| Agent | Mode | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `automatic` | continuity returns on its own after a compaction |
| Codex | `automatic` | same, once its hooks are trusted inside Codex |
| OpenCode | `agent_initiated` | a checkpoint is written; the agent asks for it |
| Any MCP client | `unavailable_automatic` | no compaction signal; checkpoint on demand |

Every one of those was established by driving a **real** compaction in the agent
and reading what Cairn recorded, not by reading an adapter.

**Capture and delivery are different capabilities.** Being told a compaction
happened says nothing about whether anything can be handed back. Cairn now
models those as two capabilities, and `automatic` requires that Cairn has
*observed* a delivery on your machine. A vendor's documentation is not evidence,
so a mistake in Cairn's own table can only ever under-promise. This is the same
principle as alpha.4's level derivation, applied to continuity.

**Divergence is reported before anything else.** A restored checkpoint that was
recorded against a commit, task state or file that has since moved leads with
that fact, and its recorded action is labelled **previous**, never `next`. A
stale next action acted on is worse than no next action at all.

## Supported platforms

| Platform | Status |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon, `aarch64-apple-darwin`) | Supported |
| macOS (Intel, `x86_64-apple-darwin`) | Supported |
| Linux (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`) | Supported |
| Linux (`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`) | Supported |
| Windows (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) | Supported |

The integration suites run on all three operating systems in CI.

## Upgrading from alpha.4

`cairn update` fetches and replaces both binaries for you. It does not restart
the daemon — it prints the two commands below, and you run them:

```bash
cairn daemon stop && cairn daemon start
```

Your local state is kept. Data written by alpha.4 remains readable, and existing
integrations are adopted rather than replaced. The local store gains one
migration, applied on first start.

Continuity modes are re-derived from what Cairn observes on your machine, so an
agent may report `agent_initiated` until it has been through one compaction here
— that is the honest answer, not a regression. To see where each agent stands:

```bash
cairn agents
cairn doctor
```

Codex specifically: its hooks must be trusted once inside Codex before its
handlers run. Cairn now reads that trust from Codex's own configuration, so an
approval you have already given is recognised.

## Install

Download the archive for your platform, verify it, and put the binaries on your
PATH. `cairn` and `cairnd` must live in the same directory — `cairn` starts the
daemon itself.

macOS and Linux:

```bash
VERSION=0.1.0-alpha.5
TARGET=aarch64-apple-darwin   # or x86_64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu

curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v${VERSION}/cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}.tar.gz
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v${VERSION}/SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS

tar -xzf cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}.tar.gz
sudo install -m 0755 cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}/cairn cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}/cairnd /usr/local/bin/
```

Windows, in PowerShell — the archive is a `.zip`:

```powershell
$VERSION = "0.1.0-alpha.5"
$TARGET = "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"

Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v$VERSION/cairn-v$VERSION-$TARGET.zip" -OutFile cairn.zip
Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v$VERSION/SHA256SUMS" -OutFile SHA256SUMS

Expand-Archive cairn.zip -DestinationPath .
mkdir "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Cairn" -Force
Copy-Item "cairn-v$VERSION-$TARGET\cairn.exe","cairn-v$VERSION-$TARGET\cairnd.exe" "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Cairn"
setx PATH "$env:PATH;$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Cairn"
```

Open a new terminal so the PATH change takes effect. Then, inside a Git
repository, on any platform:

```bash
cairn init
cairn agents
cairn connect claude-code   # or codex, or opencode
```

## Container images

Only the server-side components ship as images. The local agent is native by
design.

```
ghcr.io/vellixia/cairn-server:0.1.0-alpha.5
ghcr.io/vellixia/cairn-web:0.1.0-alpha.5
```

Both are also published under an immutable `sha-<short-sha>` tag and built for
`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. There is deliberately no `latest` tag for a
pre-release. An example stack is in
[`deploy/docker-compose.yml`](https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/blob/main/deploy/docker-compose.yml).

## Verifying what you downloaded

- `SHA256SUMS` covers every archive, `.tar.gz` and `.zip` alike.
- `SBOM.spdx.json` describes the release contents.
- Archives and images carry GitHub build provenance attestations:

```bash
gh attestation verify cairn-v0.1.0-alpha.5-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip --repo Vellixia/Cairn
```

## Known limitations

- **Alpha.** Expect defects. Do not depend on this for anything you cannot
  afford to lose.
- **OpenCode cannot reach `automatic`.** It publishes no post-compaction session
  open, and its compaction hook only biases the summarising model rather than
  placing text into the compacted context. `agent_initiated` is the truthful
  answer: a checkpoint is written and the agent asks for it, which always works.
  A deterministic mechanism is tracked in
  [#49](https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/issues/49).
- **OpenCode's pre-compaction capability is reported `conditional` on a
  condition that cannot be satisfied.** It understates a real capability and
  cannot cause an over-claim, but the stated condition is not actionable
  ([#50](https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/issues/50)).
- **Topic keys do not converge across agents.** Value keys do. Two agents
  recording the same fact tend to agree on the value and disagree on the
  namespace, which costs deduplication rather than correctness. Measured, with
  the numbers, in `evals/topic-key-effectiveness/`.
- **Continuity is bounded, not guaranteed, around an abandoned session.** Cairn
  has no liveness signal by design, so a session that stopped seconds ago is
  indistinguishable from one that is thinking.
